target_customer: Startups and online businesses that want to retain users with automated emails
problem: Startups lacked an easy way to send welcome, inactivity and trigger emails to keep users; Userfox bundled drip, inactivity and transactional emails in one dashboard.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription ($49 per month and $119 per month Premium tiers at launch)

founders.name: Peter Clark
previous_startups: Vimessa (YC-backed video voicemail app, shut down)
founders.background_notes: YC page: about 15 years in growth, especially for B2B companies. Led AdRoll product efforts after the acquisition per the acquisition coverage.

founders.name: Cesar Alaniz
previous_startups: Vimessa (YC-backed video voicemail app, shut down)
founders.background_notes: YC bio says previously Director of Engineering at Weebly and later at Block; the timing relative to Userfox is not stated, so no prior employer is recorded.

competitors.name: Marketo
competitors.what: Enterprise marketing automation the founders positioned against

competitors.name: MailChimp
competitors.what: Email marketing tool commonly used by startups

competitors.name: SendGrid
competitors.what: Transactional email API commonly used by startups

technical_complexity.rationale: A JavaScript snippet plus an email campaign engine and templates; TechCrunch reported two million emails per month in beta, which is routine infrastructure.

defensibility.rationale: Customer event data and configured campaigns create some lock-in, but many email tools covered the same ground.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: AdRoll bought Userfox in January 2014 rather than an email incumbent copying it.

market_need_then: At launch TechCrunch reported hundreds of customers in a quiet beta sending two million emails a month, which shows startups wanted retention email without enterprise tools.

branding.domain_note: Used userfox.com (exact .com); returned HTTP 503 when fetched.

identity.voice_and_tone: YC page: 'We're building a company. Not a product, and certainly not a feature.'

brand_strength.rationale: Launch and acquisition press only; a branding search returned only Firefox material and nothing on a Userfox mascot or logo.

outcome_analysis: Userfox came from the founders of Vimessa, a YC video voicemail app that was shut down, and launched publicly in February 2013 with $700K seed funding and hundreds of beta customers. AdRoll acquired it on 2014-01-23 and Peter Clark took on product work there. The pivot from a failed consumer app to a B2B retention tool and a quick exit within a year of launch is the documented success pattern; the price is undisclosed.
notes: YC lists batch Winter 2011 but a founder bio says S11 and the product launched in 2013 after Vimessa was shut down, so the batch and founding year conflict; as_of for competition is set to the 2013-02 launch coverage. Seedtable dates the seed 2012-01 and Dealroom puts YC's portion at $125K in 2011; TechCrunch announcement date is used and the $700K is also reported by CB Insights. The acquisition press release was seen in search results, not opened. Status Inactive is consistent with the acquisition. Pivot from Vimessa recorded as the founders' prior startup rather than a Userfox pivot.
